Kennedy Center Votes to Close
CNN 5 Things
Today
8 min
Another measles death, the most in US in decades. The latest developments in the Kennedy Center’s name change saga. There’s a major update in the case against Nick Reiner, accused of killing his parents. The FBI director clashed with lawmakers in a heated hearing today. Plus, the US just took national defense to orbit. Learn more about your ad choices. Visit podcastchoices.com/adchoices

A federal judge has blocked the Kennedy Center from moving forward with plans to add the name of President Donald Trump to the building facade and grounds, as reported by Deadline. In a ruling issued on Tuesday, U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper stated that the institution cannot proceed with these naming proposals without clear approval from Congress.
This decision marks the latest development in a long-running legal dispute over the branding of the site. The judge emphasized that the law limits the placement of memorials within the facility to honor only President Kennedy. In his ruling, the judge wrote, “Simply put, Defendants cannot install memorials for President Trump or anyone or anything else at the Kennedy Center without Congress’s blessing.”
The board had previously voted to designate the complex as the Trump Kennedy Center, a move that prompted a legal challenge and an earlier order from Judge Cooper to remove the name. Since that initial ruling last spring, a tarp has remained over the official designation on the front of the building. The board attempted to circumvent this by proposing new signage that would state the center was “Restored and Renovated by President Donald J. Trump” and by renaming the surrounding grounds as “President Donald J. Trump Plaza.”
Judge Cooper noted that the law specifically prohibits additional memorials in public areas
Judge Cooper noted that “common sense dictates that the words ‘renovated and restored by President Donald J. Trump’ establish a memorial.” Regarding the proposal to rename the grounds, the judge observed that Congress likely did not intend for the board to sell off naming rights to parts of the campus.
The board has argued that adding the president’s name is a vital strategy to raise funds and avoid bankruptcy. However, Judge Cooper pointed out that the center’s attorneys failed to provide evidence supporting the claim that such branding would help. Instead, he noted that the court saw data suggesting the opposite, including declining ticket sales, the departure of the Washington National Opera, and the cancellation of performances by artists who disagreed with the name change.
President Trump addressed the ruling on Truth Social, describing the center as being in a “virtual state of collapse.” He stated, “The Board of The Kennedy Center has strongly voted to save it, and they know I’m the only one who can do so, because I have the ability to raise the money, and the ability to construct — that few others have.” He further claimed that the building is “destined to doom” due to the court’s interference.
The board had also been considering a resolution to immediately close the main building, citing safety concerns following a ceiling collapse during a rainstorm. While the judge did not block a potential closure, he previously required the board to conduct a more thorough assessment of the impact before moving forward. The center is currently appealing the judge’s original order that prohibited the initial naming plan and required more oversight regarding renovation shutdowns.

Rep. Joyce Beatty, an ex-officio board member of the Kennedy Center who sued President Trump over his plans for the arts institution, blasted the decision to shut down the center.
On Tuesday, the board voted to shut down the Kennedy Center immediately, according to media reports and a post from Trump, which they said was to allow for renovations to the center. This vote came after a federal judge had issued an injunction earlier in the day, blocking the board from adding Trump’s name to the Kennedy Center.
The board had added his name earlier this year, but Beatty sued, seeking a court order to halt the closure of the center and reverse its name change. She issued a statement Tuesday suggesting she will bring the matter of the closure to the court.
“For years, the Kennedy Center has planned to undergo phased renovations, in which we both renovate and maintain some performances. This is how major performing arts centers in the country operate. But donors, patrons, and artists all fled after the unlawful attempt to rename this sacred memorial after Donald Trump,” Beatty said Tuesday. “Donald Trump only cares about the Kennedy Center for his vanity. That is wrong and it is a breach of his fiduciary duty as a trustee. Congress established the Kennedy Center as a living memorial to President Kennedy, and I am proud to defend this cherished institution.”
“The Board’s latest shutdown vote is more of the same failure and abuse that has characterized this administration’s treatment of the Kennedy Center,” said Rep. Beatty’s counsel, Norm Eisen (ret.) of Democracy Defenders Action and Nathaniel Zelinsky of Washington Litigation Group. “The unlawful renaming drove audiences and artists away. Now the Board has voted to shut down yet again to hide the terrible mismanagement under its current leadership. We’ll see the Defendants in court.”
In his post on Truth Social on Tuesday, Trump said the board, which he handpicked and which voted him in as chairman, voted for the immediate closure for “safety reasons” and in order to begin what he said were “large and very complex” renovations.
However, he said that he would be appealing the decision not to add his name to the building and said that these renovations would not begin without his name.
“If the ruling is a negative one, which it should not be, and is not overturned by the U.S. Supreme Court, the Reconstruction and the Renovation of The Kennedy Center will not take place,” Trump wrote.

Judge again blocks efforts to add Trump’s name to Kennedy Center
Ohio Rep. Joyce Beatty sued in December to block renaming
A federal judge on Tuesday ruled in favor of an Ohio House Democrat who is seeking to block efforts to add President Donald Trump’s name to the Kennedy Center.
In his ruling, Judge Christopher R. Cooper of the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia said that the Trump-led board of the Kennedy Center could not add Trump’s name to the building or rename the grounds after the president.
The order represents the second time Cooper has ruled in favor of Rep. Joyce Beatty, D-Ohio, an ex-officio member of the Center’s board, on changes made to the cultural institution.
“Simply put, Defendants cannot install memorials for President Trump or anyone or anything else at the Kennedy Center without Congress’s blessing. The board resolution bucks a federal court order and a statute Congress enacted,” the ruling said.
Beatty filed the lawsuit in December after a reshuffled board first voted to close the Center for two years and add Trump’s name to the marquee. She argued that the board did not follow federal law in its initial closures and that the law barred renaming the center after Trump.
Cooper first ruled against adding Trump’s name to the institution in May, finding that federal law mandated the name of the facility as the “John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts” and required that no other person be memorialized there.
Tuesday’s ruling came ahead of a planned board action to add language honoring Trump to the Center’s name and separately renaming the Center’s grounds to the “President Donald J. Trump Plaza;” it explicitly blocked those alternatives.
The board also planned to vote on whether to close the Center for two years for renovations during a meeting Tuesday. Beatty filed a court notice later in the day that said the board did vote to close the Center.
Trump, the chair of the board, later posted on social media that if the courts do not side with him and place his name on the Center, the renovations would not occur.
Court records have said that if those renovations do not go through, the Center may need to be demolished.
Beatty’s counsel Norm Eisen praised the Tuesday ruling in a statement on the social platform X.
“2 times the court has told Trump the same thing: You are not above the law. Legal sanity has once again prevailed over Trump’s vanity. This is a victory for the memory of Pres. Kennedy & our nation,” Eisen’s statement said.
Trump criticized the ruling in a post on his social media website, Truth Social, Tuesday, alleging the building was unsafe, citing a recent collapse of part of the center’s ceiling. He said millions of dollars in repairs are needed to reopen the building.
“A very hostile and conflicted Judge (What else is new?) seems like he won’t let that happen, in which case, unfortunately, the Building is destined to doom,” Trump said.
The effort by Trump and his appointees to the board come amid the president’s broader efforts to reshape official Washington in his image.
That includes tearing down and rebuilding the East Wing of the White House for a planned ballroom complex, erecting a 250-foot memorial arch and other efforts that are currently locked up in court fights.
The Trump administration has continued to fight to add his name to the center, including a pending appeal of Cooper’s initial May ruling.
